title: Form layout
summary: Labels in one column, fields in another, stacking on phones.
brief: At 800px: a form whose labels sit in a 100px column on the left and whose fields fill the rest, each label lined up with its field. Rows are 12px apart and the two columns are 16px apart.
The Create account button sits in the field column, under the fields, at its natural width.
At 375px every label sits directly above its field and the button starts at the left edge.
hints: The labels and fields are siblings, alternating: label, field, label, field. That is a two-column grid filling row by row.
grid-template-columns: 100px 1fr on .form, with gap: 12px 16px and align-items: center so each label lines up with its field.

The button is a single child, so it lands in the label column. Send it to the second column with grid-column: 2, and stop it stretching with justify-self: start. For phones, one column, and grid-column: auto.
solutionNotes: Grid places children row by row, so alternating label and field fall into two columns without any wrapper. The button is the odd child out: grid-column: 2 moves it under the fields, and justify-self: start keeps it at its natural width instead of stretching across the column. On phones a single column puts every label above its field; the button must drop grid-column: 2 too, or it would create a second, implicit column.
